text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:

- Coaliton prepares for new savings package. Leading politicians in the coalition working on steps to cut spending in order to avoid increase in new borrowing. Tax estimate on Thursday expected to show revenues worse than feared.
- Government's move to Berlin could be delayed to after 2000. Remarks inside the government by parliament and government leaders suggest delay from 1999 to after 2000 being considered.
- Government cabinet decides to continue support programme for eastern Germany for another six years.

- Finance Minister Theo Waigel wants to sell a portion of the government's two billion shares in Deutsche Telekom on the stock market before the year 2000, as originally planned. Waigel would use the proceeds from the sale to reduce new debt.

- Deutsche Telekom's profit doubled in 1996. Company chairman Ron Sommer says he expects 1997 to be even more successful for the telcommunications giant. Says net profid should more than double this year.

- Dispute in the FDP escalates over Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt. Former economics Minister Juergen Moellemann says several FDP ministers in the coalition should be replaced. He urges Rexrodt to resign.
- Consumer prices in April up 1.4 percent from year earlier. That was down slightly from the 1.5 percent annual rise posted in March.

- Coalition will have an emergency meeting on Thursday evening to discuss the difficult financial situation. The coalition members will be informed about the tax estimates, which are expected to show diminished revenues.
- Next general elections should be held on September 27, 1998 - that is what leaders in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coaliton government want.
- Construction employers willing to talk with construction workers about narrowing their differences over a disputed pay deal. - Bonn Newsroom, 49 228 260 97160
